footer.lead: OpenDefence is an FDF-serving national defence open-source project that aims to offer multi-domain-operation-capable C2 services to soldiers in an easy and interoperable way.
footer.lead2: The cornerstone of the project is Deploy App, which accepts product integrations, defines how to spin up servers with them, and lets soldiers easily use them.
footer.core: The core of the OpenDefence stack is Deploy App. For users, it's best described as an app for adding and managing users; for developers, as an interface to integrate your application with — to get it into the hands of soldiers.
footer.easyBody: Deploy App aims to give soldiers the ability to easily gain, manage and share access to their unit's services. Using Deploy App and the services behind it should be so easy that no special training is needed.
footer.interopBody: For us, interoperability is not a marketing slogan. Deploy App offers app developers an integration interface: integrate your product into Deploy App, and Deploy App operators can deploy it to soldiers — working together with the other products.
footer.maintain: OpenDefence develops and maintains a couple of official product integrations and user guides, as shown here. The products themselves are made by their original developers, such as the TAK Product Center. Our official product integrations adhere to our goals and values.
footer.readMore: Read more about OpenDefence, the vision and how to contribute:
footer.qualityTitle: Goal of great quality and security
footer.qualityBody: Deploy App and all official product integrations must withstand actual war — nothing less. That demands paramount quality, simplicity and reality-based security. We don't develop or release features that fall short of these standards; we'd rather go without them.

guidesFooter.lead: Deploy App has a number of official product integrations, each currently developed by OpenDefence. Here you can find guides to use the official products efficiently.
guidesFooter.devBody: We develop product integrations for Deploy App to give soldiers a strong stack of services. These integrations are open source, just like core Deploy App — and you are invited to collaborate with us.
guidesFooter.wantTitle: Want to see your product here?
guidesFooter.wantBody: OpenDefence aims to make Deploy App a true interface for deploying apps to soldiers. That works when you can fork our core, build your integration yourself, and then either contact us for official integration status or agree to deliver your app to your armed-forces customer on our open-source tech.

products.tak: Developed by the TAK Product Center (TPC), a U.S. Government organization. The OpenDefence-developed integration gets your ATAK users connected to the server by a double-tap self service — yes, press two buttons and you're in.
products.matrix: An open, decentralized messaging protocol from the Matrix.org Foundation; clients such as Element X are spearheaded by New Vector Ltd. The OpenDefence-developed integration lets users connect their Element X client to the Deploy App-bundled Synapse server by simply pasting in the server address.
products.mediamtx: A real-time media server: a video-sharing service that lets you quickly share video from e.g. drone operators. The OpenDefence-developed integration lets you start streaming with your OpenTAK ICU and UAS Tool applications by tapping an import-settings button once.
products.cryptpad: Developed by XWiki SAS, CryptPad is an end-to-end-encrypted collaboration and file-sharing suite used by, among others, the European Commission.

tak-guide.lead: TAK (Team Awareness Kit) is the U.S. Government's battle-tested situational awareness platform, giving soldiers a shared operational picture across Android, iOS, and Windows devices in the field.
tak-guide.core: The OpenDefence TAK integration makes TAK servers deployable through Deploy App and puts step-by-step guidance directly in soldiers' hands — covering client setup, server configuration, and day-to-day operations.
tak-guide.goal1Body: TAK puts every unit member on the same map in real time. The OpenDefence integration ensures the server side is set up correctly and consistently so the picture is always accurate when it matters most.
tak-guide.goal2Body: ATAK, iTAK, and WinTAK each have their own setup flows. This guide walks through each client so no soldier is left behind regardless of their device.
tak-guide.goal3Body: Every step in this guide has been validated in real deployment scenarios. Nothing is included unless it works reliably under operational conditions.
tak-guide.copyright: TAK: © TAK Product Center, a U.S. Government organization

mtx-guide.lead: MediaMTX is a zero-dependency media server and proxy that handles RTSP, RTMP, HLS, WebRTC, and SRT streams — purpose-built for latency-sensitive video in field environments.
mtx-guide.core: The OpenDefence MediaMTX integration provides a Deploy App-compatible media server deployment and a concise guide for getting live video from field cameras into soldiers' devices with minimal configuration.
mtx-guide.goal1Body: Sub-second latency matters when the feed is a UAV over a contested area. MediaMTX achieves this out of the box; the integration keeps the configuration path as short as possible.
mtx-guide.goal2Body: Different clients support different protocols. MediaMTX bridges RTSP sources to WebRTC viewers without additional transcoding, keeping CPU usage minimal on field hardware.
mtx-guide.goal3Body: A single container, a few configuration lines, and the stream is live. The guide covers both initial setup and common troubleshooting so operators can resolve issues without specialist help.

matrix-guide.lead: Matrix is an open standard for secure, decentralised real-time communication — giving soldiers end-to-end encrypted messaging and voice that works across organisations without a central authority.
matrix-guide.core: The OpenDefence Matrix integration deploys a Synapse homeserver through Deploy App and guides users through client setup, room creation, and cross-server federation for inter-unit communication.
matrix-guide.goal1Body: Your unit's messages stay on your server. Federation lets you communicate with other units' servers without giving any single organisation control over the whole network.
matrix-guide.goal2Body: Matrix's E2EE means even the homeserver operator cannot read message content. This guide covers key verification steps so encryption is genuinely end-to-end in practice, not just in theory.
matrix-guide.goal3Body: Matrix homeservers are designed to survive network partitions and reconnect gracefully. The deployment configuration in this guide is tuned for intermittent connectivity typical in field operations.

deploy-app.lead: Deploy App is the heart of the OpenDefence stack — the interface through which operators deploy services to soldiers and through which soldiers access everything from a single, familiar place.
deploy-app.core: This guide covers Deploy App from both sides: soldiers learning to get access and manage their accounts, and operators managing users, roles, and service deployments across their unit.
deploy-app.goal1Body: A soldier picking up Deploy App for the first time should be able to log in and reach their unit's services without reading a manual. Every flow is designed with that bar in mind.
deploy-app.goal2Body: Operators get fine-grained control over who accesses what, with audit trails and role management that meet the accountability requirements of military operations.
deploy-app.goal3Body: Every official OpenDefence product integrates through Deploy App. Adding a new service is a configuration task, not a development task — operators can deploy approved integrations in minutes.

atak.lead: ATAK is the flagship application of the TAK ecosystem. There are a few so-called flavors of ATAK — CIVTAK, MilTAK, and national TAK apps. They are the same application, but they accept only specifically signed plugins: a MilTAK installation will accept MilTAK-signed plugins and reject others.

itak.lead: iTAK is the iOS version of ATAK, bringing the full TAK situational awareness experience to iPhone and iPad. It shares the same server protocols and data formats as ATAK, so ATAK and iTAK users see each other on the same map.

wintak.lead: WinTAK is the Windows desktop client for the TAK ecosystem, designed for use in command posts and operations centers where a full-screen map interface and keyboard-driven workflow are preferred over a mobile device.
